repo_model.summary: This repository is a RelBench generic-search starter candidate: main.py loads the configured task and emits NumPy prediction files for recommendation, classification, or regression tasks, while the provided contract helpers and grader validate and officially score the predictions.

entrypoints.how_to_run: python main.py --debug for the fast contract check, or python main.py for the full training run.

evidence.description: Shows that fast mode appends --debug and full mode does not.

where_to_edit.role: Primary solution file: replace the trivial task-family prediction logic with feature construction, training, validation prediction, and test prediction.

evidence.description: Identifies the file as a baseline candidate.
Explicitly instructs replacing the baseline with a real solution.
Contains the current prediction logic to replace.

where_to_edit.role: Reusable helper module for loading RelBench context, saving contract-compliant predictions, guarding temporal leakage, and calculating MAP@K.

evidence.description: States that the starter kit provides contract helpers.
Shows the intended helper imports for main.py.

where_to_edit.role: Provided immutable scoring pipeline; do not reimplement or modify it.

evidence.description: Describes grader.py as the complete immutable scoring pipeline.
Instructs users not to modify files under kapso_evaluation.

claims.statement: main.py is the candidate workflow: it reads the dataset/task identity, loads the RelBench task without downloading, determines validation and test row counts, constructs predictions, and writes NumPy artifacts.

evidence.description: Reads the required dataset environment variable.

claims.statement: Prediction generation branches by task family: recommendations repeat destination ids 0 through eval_k-1, binary classification uses 0.5 probabilities, multiclass classification uses uniform class scores, and other tasks use the training target median.

evidence.description: Falls back to the non-classification prediction path.

claims.statement: kapso_datasets/common.py provides an optional task context layer that loads the dataset, database, and train/validation/test tables, plus helpers for saving predictions, checking temporal safety, and evaluating recommendation MAP@K.

evidence.description: Obtains the database with the requested timestamp cutoff.
Loads the train, validation, and test tables.

claims.statement: kapso_evaluation/grader.py runs main.py in an isolated child process, loads the resulting validation predictions, computes official RelBench validation metrics, and archives full-fidelity runs for final selection.
The candidate must use the configured RelBench dataset and task, access the sanitized cache with download=False, and write outputs under KAPSO_RUN_DATA_DIR.

evidence.description: Requires download=False and prohibits probing for test labels.

claims.statement: Validation and test prediction rows must remain positionally aligned with task.get_table('val') and task.get_table('test'); validation predictions must be out-of-sample and must not be trained on validation labels.

evidence.description: Requires both prediction files after every normal run.
Requires validation predictions to be out-of-sample.
Permits train-plus-validation only for the model producing test predictions.

claims.statement: Required output formats are binary float probabilities of shape (N,), regression floats of shape (N,), multiclass float scores of shape (N,C), and recommendation integer rankings of shape (N,K) containing distinct destination ids in range [0, num_dst).

evidence.description: Defines binary and regression output requirements.
Defines multiclass and recommendation shape/type requirements.
Defines recommendation id range and distinctness requirements.

claims.statement: The search score of record is the official primary validation metric; test metrics are private and unavailable in the sanitized evaluation loop.

evidence.description: Defines the official validation primary metric as the search score.
States that test metrics are computed privately.
Places the primary validation metric in the manifest score.

claims.statement: A normal candidate invocation must produce both val_predictions.npy and test_predictions.npy, and the checker requires finite non-recommendation values.

evidence.description: Requires both files after every run.
Checks both validation and test splits.

claims.statement: The fastest end-to-end sanity check is python main.py --debug; the full candidate run is python main.py, and both are expected to complete while producing the required artifacts.

evidence.description: States that outputs are loaded, validated, and scored after each run.

claims.statement: After writing predictions, run python kapso_datasets/check_predictions.py to catch missing files, shape mismatches, invalid dtypes, non-finite values, and binary probabilities outside [0,1].

evidence.description: Fails when a prediction file is missing.

claims.statement: Official evaluation prints OFFICIAL VALIDATION METRICS and a KAPSO_EVAL_MANIFEST line containing the fidelity, item counts, and score; fast mode still scores the complete validation split rather than a reduced sample.

evidence.description: Defines fast fidelity as the debug candidate build.
States that the complete validation split is always scored.
Prints the manifest marker and score.

claims.statement: Rolling evaluation ticks are special: main.py detects an empty validation snapshot, omits val_predictions.npy for that tick, and writes only test predictions; the rolling grader later assembles per-tick test outputs into the official vectors.

evidence.description: Documents the empty validation table in rolling snapshots.
Sets the validation row count to zero when the validation file is absent.
Determines rolling mode from the validation row count.
Suppresses validation output in rolling mode.
Loads each tick's test prediction file.
Writes the assembled official prediction vector.

claims.statement: The checked-in candidate is intentionally trivial: recommendations always use the first eval_k ids, classifiers use constant or uniform scores, and other tasks use the training median; --debug is only reflected in the status output rather than changing the prediction logic.

evidence.description: Describes the outputs as trivial predictions.
Uses the training median for the fallback.
Uses --debug in the printed diagnostic field.

claims.statement: Recommendation ids outside the destination range or duplicate ids are reported as warnings by the local checker rather than immediate failures, even though the evaluation contract requires valid distinct in-range rankings.

evidence.description: Reports out-of-range ids as a warning.
Reports duplicate ids as a warning.

claims.statement: Test labels are physically absent from the sanitized cache, so test predictions are artifacts only during the search loop and must not be used for local label probing or score optimization.

evidence.description: States that test metrics are private.
States that test labels are physically absent.
States that test predictions cannot be scored in the loop.

claims.statement: The candidate directly depends on NumPy and RelBench task APIs, including RecommendationTask, TaskType, and get_task.

evidence.description: States that Python with relbench and numpy is sufficient.

claims.statement: Configuration is supplied through environment variables including RELBENCH_DATASET, RELBENCH_TASK, RELBENCH_PRIMARY_METRIC, RELBENCH_CACHE_DIR, RELBENCH_WORK_DIR, debug/full timeouts, and KAPSO_SHARED_CACHE_DIR.

evidence.description: Lists dataset and task identity variables.
Lists the primary metric and archive root.
Lists the debug and full timeout variables.
Lists the shared candidate cache variable.

claims.statement: RelBench data access is offline and cache-backed: helpers load the dataset and task with download=False and obtain the database from the configured sanitized cache.

evidence.description: Obtains the database from the loaded dataset.
Requires download=False and describes the sanitized read-only cache.

book.summary: This repository is a RelBench generic-search starter candidate: main.py loads the configured task and emits NumPy prediction files for recommendation, classification, or regression tasks, while the provided contract helpers and grader validate and officially score the predictions.

toc.title: Architecture
toc.one_liner: Single candidate entrypoint with task-family prediction dispatch and an isolated official evaluator.

toc.title: Entrypoints
toc.one_liner: Run the candidate directly for debug or full mode, or invoke the provided grader for official scoring.

toc.title: Where to edit
toc.one_liner: Implement the candidate in main.py and optionally reuse or extend the starter helpers; leave the provided evaluator immutable.

toc.title: Invariants
toc.one_liner: Prediction artifacts must obey strict split alignment, task-specific shape/type, and validation-scoring contracts.

toc.title: Testing
toc.one_liner: Use debug mode for a fast end-to-end check, the prediction checker for local validation, and the grader manifest for official scoring.

toc.title: Gotchas
toc.one_liner: Rolling snapshots, baseline defaults, and recommendation warnings can differ from ordinary full-run behavior.

toc.title: Dependencies
toc.one_liner: Runtime depends on Python with NumPy and RelBench, configured through exported dataset, cache, output, metric, and timeout variables.
